quote: oscillate more times per mean spacing of the zeros and their combined omitted contribution matters more
problem: Backwards. The mean spacing of the zeros is 2π/log(t/2π), which shrinks as t grows, so a wave of fixed frequency log q completes log q/log(t/2π) cycles per mean spacing: fewer at larger t, not more.
fix: Replace with: 'at larger t the mean spacing 2π/log(t/2π) shrinks, so a wave sin(t log q) completes only log q/log(t/2π) cycles per spacing; more prime powers (roughly those with q below t/2π) then vary slowly on the scale of one spacing and shift individual zeros coherently, so a fixed prime set leaves out more of what matters (heuristic).'

quote: In every case computed directly (including all of \cref{tab:primes-pi}), $\pi(x)<\mathrm{Li}(x)$.
problem: False for the chapter's own Li (integral from 2). Li(2)=0<π(2)=1, and π(x)>Li(x) at x=2,3,5,7 (e.g. Li(7)≈3.71<4). So 'No sign change has been found' is also false as written. The classical statement and Littlewood's theorem concern li(x)=∫_0^x.
fix: State the comparison for li(x)=Li(x)+1.045: 'In every case computed directly, π(x)<li(x) for x≥2', and phrase Littlewood's theorem and the first-sign-change bound for π(x)−li(x). Alternatively restrict the Li statement to x≥11.

quote: Both approximations are asymptotically correct, but $\mathrm{Li}$ is far better at every height we can check.
problem: Contradicted by Table tab:primes-pi. At x=10 the errors are +0.34 (x/log x) vs +1.12 (Li); at x=100 they are −3.3 vs +4.1. Li is the worse approximation at both.
fix: Replace with: 'Both are asymptotically correct; from x=10^3 upward in our table Li is far better (at x=10 and 100 it is not).'

quote: is within a fraction of a percent of 1 over most of the range
problem: π(x)/Li(x) is 0.78 at x=10, 0.86 at 100, 0.951 at 10^3 and 0.987 at 10^4. It is within 1% only above a few times 10^4, a minority of the logarithmic axis shown.
fix: Write: 'π(x)/Li(x) is within 2% of 1 from x=10^4 on and within 0.2% at 10^6, while π(x)/(x/log x) is still about 1.08 at x=10^6.'

quote: (close to the staircase). At $x=100$ the three values are $25$, $21.7$ and $29.1$.
problem: The caption calls Li 'close to the staircase', but the values it quotes show Li is farther from π(100)=25 (off by 4.1) than x/log x is (off by 3.3). Over 2≤x≤100, Li is not visibly the closer curve.
fix: Change to '(above the staircase over most of this range)' and add that Li's advantage only shows at larger x (see fig:primes-ratio).

quote: \begin{didyouknow}{Euclid's Endless Primes}

It is used three times and will not compile unless added to the preamble. Its facts (dates, digit count) are also not covered by CHECKS.

quote: Red: the 18 terms of the six-prime explicit formula ($p\le13$, $m\le3$).
problem: The figure shows only q≤200, but three of the 18 terms (7^3=343, 11^3=1331, 13^3=2197) exceed 200. At most 15 red lines can appear. The same applies to the 'blue' 25-prime terms.
fix: Say 'Red: the 15 of the 18 six-prime terms with q≤200 (343, 1331 and 2197 lie off the plot)', or extend the frequency axis to log 2197≈7.7.

quote: when $\abs{\omega-\log q}<\pi/T$. There are $466$ prime powers up to $3000$
problem: T is never defined in this chapter. It is the length of the training window in t, and the bible notes T is overloaded. 'Half the Fourier resolution' and '2π/T' are used with no definition or number, so the student cannot judge the crowding argument.
fix: Add: 'Here T is the length in t of the training window (about 1170 for zeros 1–800, so π/T≈0.003 and the full window 2π/T≈0.005); Chapter~\ref{ch:fourier-transform} derives the resolution 2π/T.' Compute these values in CHECKS.

quote: This is one reason the paper does not rest the alignment claim on matches alone
problem: This attributes a motive to the paper that it does not state. The paper's stated reason for the surrogate check is 'Because the frequencies are the output of a search'; it does not mention crowding of log q.
fix: Rephrase: 'The paper gives its own reason for the surrogate check (the frequencies are the output of a search). The crowding of log q, our observation, is a further reason why matches alone would be weak evidence.'

quote: $\psi(x)-x$ fluctuates on the scale $\sqrt x$; the von Mangoldt explicit formula writes it as a sum over the zeta zeros.
problem: Stated as fact with no status. That ψ(x)−x is of size about √x is a numerical observation for x≤10^5. It is known only conditionally (RH gives O(√x log²x)); unconditionally only the far weaker de la Vallée Poussin bound is proved. The same unlabelled claim is in the text before tab:primes-psi and in the fig:primes-psi caption.
fix: Label it: 'Numerically (x≤10^5), ψ(x)−x fluctuates on the scale √x; a bound O(√x log²x) for all x is equivalent to the Riemann hypothesis (open).' Add the same qualifier in the caption and running text.

quote: and the argument used nothing but factorization
problem: The Chebyshev theorem is labelled 'Theorem (proved)', yet steps 1 and 2 use Euclid's lemma, which the chapter took on trust in a beyond box. The status should be stated consistently.
fix: Write 'proved, given Euclid's lemma (taken on trust in \cref{sec:primes-fta})' in the theorem header and here.

quote: Table~V's columns are the sets $P=\{2\}$; ``3 primes'' $=\{2,3,5\}$
problem: The paper never lists the prime sets for '3 primes', '6 primes', '25 primes'. That they are the first k primes is an inference, and CHECKS verifies it only for 6 primes.
fix: Add 'which we take to be the first k primes; the paper does not list them, but this choice reproduces its numbers (checked with qmnt)'. Add qmnt checks for the {2}, 3-prime and 25-prime entries of the 401–500 row.

quote: The cutoff is natural because C2 searches $0.05<\omega<8$
problem: The paper gives no reason for the cutoff q≤3000; presenting e^8≈2981 as the reason reads as a statement about the paper.
fix: Write 'A plausible reason for the cutoff (ours; the paper does not give one) is that C2 searches 0.05<ω<8 and e^8≈2981.'

quote: Step 3 also tells us \emph{how fast} the ratio approaches 1: the correction is of relative size $1/\log x$
problem: Step 3 only gives an upper bound of about 4/log x, not that the correction is 1/log x. The text then compares this Li-vs-x/log x correction with the excess of π(x) over x/log x, mixing two different quantities without saying π≈Li.
fix: Say: 'Step 3 bounds the relative correction by about 4/log x; the asymptotic series below shows it is in fact ≈1/log x. Since π(x)≈Li(x), π(x) exceeds x/log x by about the same fraction: 1/log x≈0.072 at 10^6, against the observed 8%.'

quote: The left side becomes a product of $r-1$ primes, the right side a product of $s-1$ primes
problem: The induction step does not treat s=1 with r≥2. After cancelling, the right side is the empty product 1, which is not 'a product of primes', so the induction hypothesis does not apply.
fix: Add before cancelling: 'If s=1 then q_1=p_1p_2\cdots p_r with r≥2 would make the prime q_1 composite, so s≥2 and both sides remain nonempty products after cancelling.'

quote: We show by induction on $r$ that the two lists are the same up to order.
problem: Proof by induction is not in the reader's stated background and is used here without explanation, whereas well-ordering was explained.
fix: Add one sentence: 'Induction means: prove the statement for r=1, then show that its truth for r−1 forces its truth for r; it then holds for every r.'

quote: (because $p$ is the \emph{smallest} prime divisor of $n$, so every prime factor of $c$ is at least $p$)
problem: Lemma 2 only supplies some prime divisor p≤√n, not the smallest one; the parenthesis silently changes which p is meant.
fix: Write 'let p be the smallest prime divisor of n; by Lemma 2, p≤√n≤√x. Then c=n/p≥√n≥p, so n≥p^2 ...'.

quote: \textbf{Corollary (proved): $\pi(x)=\order(x/\log x)$.}
problem: The derived bound is √x+(8 log 2)x/log x. The step from this to O(x/log x), which needs √x=O(x/log x), is not stated.
fix: Add: 'Since √x≤x/log x for x>1 (because log x≤√x), the right side is at most (1+8\log2)\,x/\log x, which is the O-statement.'

quote: So for any $s$ for which the sums converge (Chapter~\ref{ch:series}; $\Re s>1$ suffices),
problem: Regrouping a double sum over (p,m) into a single sum over n requires absolute convergence, not mere convergence.
fix: Write 'for any s for which the sums converge absolutely (so that terms may be regrouped, Chapter~\ref{ch:series}); Re s>1 suffices because |p^{-ms}/m|≤p^{-m\,\Re s}'.

quote: On the line $s=\tfrac12+it$ the term $n^{-s}=n^{-1/2}e^{-it\log n}$ is a wave of frequency $\log n$
problem: The identity just above was justified only for Re s>1. The text moves to the critical line with no warning here that the sum does not converge there; the caveat comes only later.
fix: Add: '(Each term makes sense on this line, but the sum itself no longer converges there; see \cref{sec:primes-paper} and Chapter~\ref{ch:explicit-formula}.)'

quote: contributes a wave $x^{1/2}e^{it_n\log x}$ in the variable $\log x$, of size $\sqrt x$
problem: The term is x^ρ/ρ, so its size is √x/|ρ_n|≈√x/t_n, not √x. The statement also assumes the zero lies on the critical line without saying so.
fix: Write 'contributes (for a zero on the critical line) a wave x^{1/2}e^{it_n\log x}/\rho_n in the variable log x, of size \sqrt x/\abs{\rho_n}'.

problem: The four displayed numbers add to 8.5251, not 8.5252 (the latter is the true log 5040 rounded). The same mismatch occurs in the ψ(30) sample: the ten displayed terms add to 28.4764, not 28.4765.
fix: Add '(the last digit differs from the sum of the rounded terms because of rounding)', or carry five decimals in the terms.

quote: Do not stop trial division at $\sqrt n$ \emph{rounded down to a prime you like}
problem: The phrase is obscure; the student cannot tell which mistake is being warned against.

quote: (that power must be divisible, and no larger power of $p$ is needed)

fix: Replace with: '(p^m is itself one of the numbers 1,…,N, so the lcm must be divisible by it; and no number ≤N is divisible by p^{m+1}>N, so no higher power is needed)'.

problem: 'It' grammatically refers to Eq. (4), the subject of the previous clause, but the intended subject is C2's list.
